import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './AppearanceControl.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Lets a person choose light, automatic or dark appearance."
/>

# AppearanceControl

`AppearanceControl` lets a person choose Light, Auto or Dark. It reads and updates the nearest `BreezeProvider`, which resolves Auto against the operating system preference.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

The application owns persistence. Save the value reported by `BreezeProvider` and pass it back as `appearance` on the next visit; `AppearanceControl` does not read or write browser storage.

## Theme-reactive shadows

Shadows use CSS variables so they change with the resolved appearance alongside colours and native controls.

<Canvas of={Stories.ThemeReactiveShadow} />

## API

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Default} />

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Marks a short status or count." />

# Badge

`Badge` is compact, non-interactive status content. Its `neutral`, `brand`, `positive`, `warning` and `danger` variants are Badge treatments—not shared control variants.

<Canvas of={Stories.Treatments} />

## Accessibility

Keep wording meaningful without colour. Do not put controls inside a badge, and do not use it for long prose.

## Loading

Set `loading` to preserve the badge shape while its status text is unavailable.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## API

actions-button--docs.name: Docs
actions-button--docs.title: Actions/Button
actions-button--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Button.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Performs an action or submits a form." />

# Button

Buttons let users perform an action, such as saving a record or submitting a form.

## Basic button

`Button` comes with four variants: `primary` (default), `secondary`, `quiet` and `danger`. The `children` prop sets the visible label.

<Canvas of={Stories.Primary} />

## Secondary button

Secondary buttons are neutral alternatives to the primary action, such as cancelling.

<Canvas of={Stories.Secondary} />

## Quiet button

Quiet buttons are low emphasis, for actions that sit alongside content.

<Canvas of={Stories.Quiet} />

## Danger button

Danger buttons are destructive actions. Use a label that states what will be removed.

<Canvas of={Stories.Danger} />

## Sizes

`size` accepts `sm`, `md` (default) and `lg`, with minimum heights of 34, 38 and 52px.

<Canvas of={Stories.TreatmentsAndSizes} />

Labels wrap and increase the height of the button:

<Canvas of={Stories.LongLabel} />

## Loading

Set `loading` while the action is in progress. The label is replaced by a skeleton, and the button cannot be activated again.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## Disabled

`disabled` prevents activation and removes the button from the tab order.

<Canvas of={Stories.Disabled} />

## Handling actions

`onAction` is called when the button is activated, and takes no arguments.

<Canvas of={Stories.Activation} />

## Form submission

Use `type="submit"` to submit the containing form, and handle submission on the form. The default is `type="button"`. The `form`, `name` and `value` props are available for form association.

## Accessibility

The label provides the accessible name and is retained while the button is loading. Buttons receive a 44px minimum target on touch devices, and `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup` are supported.

## API

<ArgTypes />

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Card.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Decorates related content as a bordered Breeze panel."
/>

# Card

`Card` groups related non-interactive content on a surface with panel elevation. Padding is selected from the Breeze spacing scale.

<Canvas of={Stories.Surface} />

## Raised cards

Use `raised` for a group nested inside another surface, not to create stronger elevation.

<Canvas of={Stories.Raised} />

## Accessibility

Cards do not become interactive. Use `article`, `aside` or `section` only when that semantic grouping is meaningful, and provide a label where the element creates a region.

Loading belongs to the content inside the card. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so placeholders match the final content structure.

## API

<ArgTypes />

# Container

`Container` caps and centres page or reading content. The page width includes 16px inline padding below `md` and 28px at and above it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Page} />

## Reading widths

Use `read` for longer explanatory text and `prose` for compact supporting copy.

<Canvas of={Stories.Reading} />

## Accessibility

Use `element="main"` only once per page. Label multiple navigation or region containers so they can be distinguished.

Loading belongs to the content inside the container. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so placeholders match the final page structure.

## API

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Grid.stories';

<Meta of={Stories} summary="Arranges content in equal, responsive columns." />

# Grid

`Grid` provides one, two or three equal columns on the Breeze spacing scale. Multi-column grids collapse to one column below `md` by default.

<Canvas of={Stories.Responsive} />

## Fixed columns

Set `collapseBelow="none"` only for content that remains understandable at narrow widths.

<Canvas of={Stories.Fixed} />

## Accessibility

Grid changes visual arrangement, not reading order. Author children in the order they should be read.

Loading belongs to the items inside the grid. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so each placeholder matches its final item.

## API

<ArgTypes />

# Inline

`Inline` lays related items out horizontally. Its gap, alignment and distribution choices are closed to the arrangements used by Breeze.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Wrapping

Enable `wrap` for collections of labels or actions that may not fit on one line.

<Canvas of={Stories.Wrapped} />

## Accessibility

Choose a semantic element only when the content forms a landmark or labelled region. Visual order and document order remain the same.

Loading belongs to the items inside the row. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so placeholders retain the intended item sizes.

# Stack

`Stack` arranges related content vertically. Choose `gap` from the 4px Breeze spacing scale and use `horizontalAlign` to align the children across the row axis.

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Alignment

The default stretches children. Use `start`, `center` or `end` when their intrinsic width should be retained.

<Canvas of={Stories.Centred} />

## Accessibility

The default `div` adds no semantics. Select `main`, `nav` or `section` only when the content has that meaning, and label landmarks or regions with `aria-label`.

Loading belongs to the items inside the stack. Compose loading-capable children or explicit `Skeleton` elements so placeholders match the final vertical rhythm.

## API

content-typography--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './Typography.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Applies Breeze text roles and locale-aware formatting."
/>

# Typography

`Typography` provides the money, heading, title, body, caption, label and micro roles. Money uses negative tracking and tabular numerals. Set `numeric` on other figure text; interface text retains normal tracking.

<Canvas of={Stories.Roles} />

## Numeric figures

Set `numeric` on figures outside the money role. They gain tabular numerals, negative tracking and logical end alignment without tightening interface headings.

<Canvas of={Stories.FiguresAndInterfaceText} />

## Money and dates

Pass semantic values with `format="currency"` or `format="date"`. Dates use the exported `IsoCalendarDate` string contract. Formatting uses the nearest `BreezeProvider` locale. Currency signs retain that locale's placement and use a true minus character.

<Canvas of={Stories.Formatting} />

No separate formatting components are exported.

## Accessibility

Choose the `element` for document semantics; the visual role does not force a heading level. Do not use colour alone to communicate direction or status.

## Loading

Set `loading` to preserve the text's place while its value is unavailable.

<Canvas of={Stories.Loading} />

## API

<ArgTypes />

foundation-breezeprovider--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks';
import * as Stories from './BreezeProvider.stories';

<Meta
  of={Stories}
  summary="Provides the locale, appearance and styles that Breeze UI components require."
/>

# BreezeProvider

`BreezeProvider` provides the locale, appearance and styles that Breeze UI components require. Render it once, above every Breeze UI component. Components rendered without a provider throw an error.

```tsx
<BreezeProvider locale="en-GB">
  <Button>Save changes</Button>
</BreezeProvider>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Default} />

## Locale

`locale` takes a BCP 47 language tag. It sets the `lang` attribute and the text direction of the provider's root element.

Only English (`en-GB`) messages are bundled. Supply partial `messages` to translate Breeze's loading announcement and appearance control into the provider locale. Without an override, Breeze's own text uses English and is marked `lang="en-GB"`, independently of the surrounding content's language.

```tsx
<BreezeProvider locale="fr-FR" messages={{ loading: 'Chargement' }}>
  <Button loading>Enregistrer</Button>
</BreezeProvider>
```

<Canvas of={Stories.Locale} />

## Appearance

Appearance defaults to `automatic`, which follows the operating system and keeps following it when the preference changes. The provider resolves the choice to `light` or `dark`, then applies that value and the matching `color-scheme` to the document element.

Use `defaultAppearance` when Breeze should hold the current choice in memory:

```tsx
<BreezeProvider
  defaultAppearance="automatic"
  locale="en-GB"
  onAppearanceChange={(appearance) => saveAppearance(appearance)}
>
  <App />
</BreezeProvider>
```

Use `appearance` with `onAppearanceChange` when application state controls it. `appearance` and `defaultAppearance` are mutually exclusive.

```tsx
<BreezeProvider
  appearance={appearance}
  locale="en-GB"
  onAppearanceChange={setAppearance}
>
  <App />
</BreezeProvider>
```

The provider never reads or writes durable browser storage. The application decides whether and where to persist the reported choice. If a persisted explicit choice must apply before the application starts, stamp its resolved value on the document element before loading the stylesheet; the stylesheet's media-query default already handles automatic dark mode before script runs.

## API

<ArgTypes />
